candidates: When writing Storybook play functions that interact with a component by accessible name (e.g., `canvas.getByRole('button', { name: '…' })`), use a partial or regex name match rather than an exact string whenever the element's accessible name can change based on story globals or component state (e.g., locked vs. unlocked, disabled vs. enabled). Also guard against clicking a disabled element by checking its `disabled` attribute first and skipping or early-returning if true, so the play function does not throw for stories that exercise the locked state.

When a UI control gains a disabled or locked state, ensure ALL associated accessibility and presentation props — such as `ariaLabel`, `ariaDescription`, and `tooltip` on the shared `Select` component in `code/core/src/components/components/Select/Select.tsx` — are conditioned on that state consistently. Leaving any one of them hardcoded to an interactive description while the others are already conditional produces misleading or internally inconsistent a11y information.
